name: LinkedIn
label: 401 Redirect_uri doesn't match, but personally
summary: Sign in and posting are self-serve. Anything about ads, sales, recruiting or learning is a separate program application, with no published timeline.
verdict: An hour for sign-in and posting. Everything else is a separate application per programme, and none of them publish a timeline.
blocker: The useful APIs sit behind per-program applications, and tokens last 60 days with no refresh unless you're an approved partner.

steps.title: Create the app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal
steps.detail: From experience, the portal asks you to associate a LinkedIn Page and a Page admin approves it. The docs page we read doesn't mention this, and LinkedIn's help article refused our fetch.

steps.title: Add the self-serve products
steps.detail: On the Products tab. Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect gives profile and email. Share on LinkedIn gives w_member_social.

steps.title: Register redirect URLs on the Auth tab
steps.detail: Absolute and HTTPS. No fragment. Query parameters on the registered URL are dropped, so don't rely on them.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Check state on return. The token request must be form-encoded and repeat the same redirect_uri. The code lives 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marketing, Sales, Talent or Learning APIs: apply per program
steps.detail: Advertising API is added as a product and reviewed. Sales Navigator, Talent and Learning each have their own partner application. LinkedIn states no timelines on the page we read.

steps.title: Plan for 60-day tokens
steps.detail: Every access token lives 60 days. Without programmatic refresh, you re-run the authorization flow, and the user only skips consent if still logged in to LinkedIn.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 5,184,000 seconds, 60 days, for every app.
Programmatic refresh tokens go to a restricted set of partners. Everyone else repeats the authorization flow.
Consent is all or nothing. A new scope forces re-authentication, and asking for a different scope than before invalidates earlier tokens.
r_compliance and w_compliance are closed. They can't be requested.
Available scopes depend on the Products your app has been approved for.
Whether a LinkedIn Page must verify your app before it works.
nuances.note: Believed yes from practice. LinkedIn's help page blocked our fetch (robots), so unconfirmed.

nuances.text: How long any of the program applications take.
nuances.note: No timeline on the getting-access page.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri on the authorize call isn't an exact registered URL.
blockers.fix: Copy it character for character from the Auth tab.

blockers.cause: Different redirect_uri than the authorize call, or the code is older than 30 minutes.
blockers.fix: Send the same URI, and exchange the code immediately.

blockers.symptom: Scope you asked for isn't granted
blockers.cause: The product that carries it isn't enabled or approved on the app.
blockers.fix: Add the product on the Products tab, or apply to its program.

blockers.symptom: Users must reconnect every two months
blockers.cause: 60-day access tokens and no refresh token.
blockers.fix: Prompt a silent re-auth before expiry, or apply for programmatic refresh.

redirect.rule: Absolute HTTPS, no #, query strings dropped. Same URI on authorize and token calls.
